description:
The seller’s little shop is reached through an errand and a set of lost keys. Oil bottles, reused cloth and homemade food make it an extension of a neighbor’s life. The robbery hurts that life before its stolen object acquires a wider meaning.

Proposed shop detail: clean returned bottles dry upside down on a rack; the seller reuses worn sleeves around filled bottles, extending the existing opening gesture. Customers pay for oil and bring the glass back. A short delivery means he has less to sell, not that his memory has suddenly worsened. The empty rack can make a later supply interruption visible before anyone explains who caused it.

Proposed sound: glass touches the wooden rack with a small hollow note; cloth dulls it when the seller wraps a bottle. The existing seller remarks that wind through the empty bottles makes a lovely sound. That ordinary pleasure can survive a difficult visit.

Established oil errand: the seller provides the already paid-for bottle used in the great upstairs lamp.

name: The Oil Shop
